mainTopic: שבירת עצם in the קרבן פסח, and the rabbinic decree of טומאה on פיגול, נותר, and יוצא
overview: The amud opens by explaining that the איסור of breaking a bone of the קרבן פסח covers a bone with a כזית of marrow inside, even with no meat outside. A ברייתא proves this from the extra פסוק about פסח שני, so the עשה of eating does not override the לא תעשה. The גמרא then challenges this from the משנה about a limb that partly went out of its permitted area. אביי and רבינא answer the challenge. Next the גמרא quotes a משנה that פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא by rabbinic decree. It gives the reasons for the decree (suspected priests and lazy priests) and its minimum size (a כזית or a כביצה). It then asks whether the רבנן also decreed טומאה on meat that went out of its area (יוצא). Proofs from the limb משנה and from a ברייתא about moving פסח meat between groups are both pushed aside. The גמרא concludes that for פסח there is clearly no decree, because the group is careful, but for other קדשים the question ends in תיקו. The amud closes by starting a new question about the source for the איסור of carrying פסח meat out of its group, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Reinterpreting the earlier ברייתא: meat outside or marrow inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects reading the earlier ברייתא as including a bone with no meat at all. Its 'second case' is a bone with no meat outside but a כזית of marrow inside at the break.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, this is what it means: the prohibition covers both a bone that has an olive-size of meat on the outside, and a bone that has no olive-size of meat on the outside but does have an olive-size of meat (marrow) inside, right where it would be broken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a reading of an earlier ברייתא. It explains that the ברייתא's second case still involves a כזית of edible meat, just inside the bone instead of outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could have read 'a bone without a כזית of meat' as a totally empty bone. The גמרא says no: that second bone has a כזית of marrow inside at the spot of breaking. So every case in the ברייתא involves a כזית of edible material somewhere on or in the bone.

keyTerms.meaning: No, this is what it is saying (a reinterpretation formula)
An olive-bulk, the minimum halachic amount of food
On the outside
On the inside
At the place of the break

steps.confusionAlert: 'Meat' here includes מוח (marrow) inside the bone. The ברייתא's 'bone without meat' only means no meat on the outside.

phrases.english: No, this is what it is saying:
Both a bone that has on it
an olive-bulk of meat on the outside,
and a bone that does not have on it
an olive-bulk of meat on the outside,
but does have an olive-bulk of meat
on the inside, at the place of the break.
phrases.notes: He means the marrow inside the bone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers an inference drawn from a ברייתא cited on the previous amud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's second case is a bone with no edible meat at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second case is a bone with a כזית of marrow inside at the place of breaking.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the איסור covers bones with or without marrow
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the איסור of breaking a bone applies whether or not the bone has מוח. The מצוה to eat the meat is fulfilled with meat on the bone, not marrow inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: 'And you shall not break a bone in it.' This includes both a bone that has marrow and a bone that has no marrow. So how do I fulfill 'And they shall eat the meat on that night'? With the meat that is on the bone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that bones with marrow are included in the איסור of breaking. The ברייתא limits the מצוה of eating to meat that is on the outside of the bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא confirms that marrow inside a bone is significant: a bone with marrow is fully covered by the איסור. Because of that, the עשה to eat the meat does not require breaking bones. It applies only to meat you can reach without breaking.

keyTerms.meaning: Marrow inside the bone
How then do I fulfill/apply (this other פסוק)?
On top of (outside) the bone

phrases.english: And it was taught:
'And you shall not break a bone in it' —
both a bone that has marrow in it,
and a bone that has no marrow in it.
And how do I fulfill
'And they shall eat the meat on that night' —
with the meat that is on the bone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that treats marrow inside the bone as significant, in line with the reinterpretation in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That a bone with marrow is included in the איסור of שבירת עצם

steps.title: The ברייתא's counter-suggestion: maybe the עשה overrides the איסור
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests the opposite reading. Perhaps the מצוה of eating includes the marrow, so a bone with marrow may be broken, because an עשה overrides a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe the eating מצוה also includes the meat inside the bone. Then how do I apply 'You shall not break a bone'? Only to a bone without marrow. But a bone with marrow, one may break and eat. And don't be surprised, because a positive מצוה comes and overrides a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a rival reading of the two פסוקים. It sets up the question that its next line will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this suggestion, the עשה of eating would cover the marrow too. The לא תעשה would shrink to bones with no marrow. The suggestion relies on the general rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה to explain why breaking would be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only (introduces a rival reading)
He breaks and eats
And do not be surprised
A positive מצוה comes and overrides a negative prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a suggestion inside the ברייתא, not the conclusion. The ברייתא rejects it in the next line.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only
also with meat that is inside the bone,
and how do I fulfill
'And you shall not break a bone in it' —
with a bone that has no marrow,
but with a bone that has marrow —
one breaks it and eats.
And do not be surprised,
for a positive מצוה comes
and overrides a negative prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּבָשָׂר שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הָעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's first reading by proposing the reverse division of the two פסוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the עשה of eating applies only to meat on the outside of the bone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the עשה includes marrow, then עשה דוחה לא תעשה would permit breaking a bone with marrow.

steps.title: The extra פסוק in פסח שני proves bones with marrow are included
steps.stepSummary: The תורה repeats the איסור of breaking a bone for פסח שני even though it was already included. The repetition teaches that the איסור covers bones with and without marrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'nor break a bone in it' about פסח שני, there was no need to say it, because it already says 'according to all the statute of the פסח they shall do it.' So you must say it comes to teach: both a bone with marrow and a bone without marrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own suggestion with a proof from a seemingly extra פסוק. It concludes that the איסור includes bones with marrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since פסח שני already follows all the rules of פסח ראשון, repeating 'וְעֶצֶם לֹא יִשְׁבְּרוּ בוֹ' must teach something new. What it teaches is that the איסור is total, even for a bone with marrow. So the עשה does not override it, and the first reading of the ברייתא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: When it (the פסוק) says
The second פסח, brought a month later by those who missed the first
There was no need for the פסוק to state it
According to all the statute of the פסח
You must therefore say

steps.whatToRemember: The איסור of שבירת עצם in the קרבן פסח applies even to a bone with marrow. The מצוה of eating does not push it aside. This is learned from the extra פסוק about פסח שני.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key method of דרשה: a repeated rule that seems unnecessary is read as widening the איסור. Here it blocks the usual rule of עשה דוחה לא תעשה.

phrases.english: When it says
'nor shall they break a bone in it'
regarding the second פסח,
which there was no need to state,
since it was already stated
'according to all the statute of the פסח they shall do it' —
you must say
both a bone that has marrow
and a bone that has no marrow.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר וְעֶצֶם לֹא יִשְׁבְּרוּ בוֹ בְּפֶסַח שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 3 and confirms the ruling of step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That the איסור of breaking includes bones with marrow, so the עשה does not override it
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra פסוק 'וְעֶצֶם לֹא יִשְׁבְּרוּ בוֹ' (במדבר ט:יב) in פסח שני, alongside 'כְּכׇל חֻקַּת הַפֶּסַח'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Breaking any bone of the פסח is forbidden, with or without marrow.

steps.title: A משנה about a limb that partly left its permitted area
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה as the base for a challenge. Part of a limb went outside its permitted boundary, and the משנה says to cut to the bone, peel the meat to the joint, and cut there.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If part of a limb went out, one cuts down until the bone, peels the meat back until the joint, and cuts there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה it will use to attack the earlier rule. This step is setting up the next move, where the attack is actually explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The part of the limb that left its permitted area has become פסול. The part still inside is kosher, so its bone may not be broken. The משנה gives a long procedure: cut to the bone, peel all the meat to the joint, and separate the limb at the joint instead of breaking the bone.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb that partly went out of its permitted boundary
Peels (the meat off the bone)
Joint, the natural meeting point of two bones

phrases.english: They raised an objection: A limb, part of which went out,
phrases.notes: It went out of the area where the meat may be eaten, so that part became פסול.

phrases.english: one cuts until the place where he reaches the bone
and peels until he reaches the joint,
and cuts.
phrases.notes: He separates the limb at the joint, so no bone is broken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source against the rule that a bone with no meat at the breaking spot is not covered by the איסור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a limb with no כזית of meat in this place, but with meat elsewhere, is not covered by שבירת העצם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spelled out in the next step: if that rule were true, the long peeling procedure would not be needed.

steps.title: Why peel all the way to the joint?
steps.stepSummary: If a bone with no meat at the breaking spot is not covered by the איסור, the משנה should let you peel a little and break the bone there. Why require peeling all the way to the joint?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that a limb with no כזית of meat in this spot, but with meat in another spot, is not covered by breaking a bone, why do I need him to peel until the joint and cut? Let him peel a little and break it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains its challenge. According to the earlier rule, an easy shortcut should be allowed, but the משנה does not allow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the earlier rule, once you peel a small area clean of meat, breaking the bone there would not be forbidden. The משנה instead requires the long route of peeling to the joint. That suggests breaking the bone even at a meat-free spot is still אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: The איסור of breaking a bone of the קרבן פסח
Why do I need this?
A little bit
And let him break it

phrases.english: And if you say that a limb

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר בְּמָקוֹם זֶה
phrases.english: that does not have an olive-bulk of meat on it in this place
but has it in another place
is not subject to the prohibition of breaking a bone,

phrases.aramaic: לְמָה לִי דְּקוֹלֵף עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לַפֶּרֶק וְחוֹתֵךְ?
phrases.english: why do I need that he peels until he reaches the joint and cuts?
Let him peel a little of it and break it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה quoted in step 5 attacks the rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a limb with no כזית of meat at the breaking spot, but with meat elsewhere, is not covered by שבירת העצם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule were true, a shortcut would be allowed: peel a small spot and break the bone there. The משנה requires the long procedure, which implies the shortcut is forbidden.

steps.title: אביי: the bone might crack too far
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה forbids the shortcut because the bone might crack beyond the peeled spot, into the part that still has meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Because of cracking.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the rule. The משנה does not disagree with it; it only worries about a practical danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking a bone at a meat-free spot really is allowed. The concern is that the crack will spread into the part of the bone that still has meat on it, and breaking there is forbidden. The משנה's long procedure is a safety measure, not a sign that the rule is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Cracking or splitting that spreads along the bone

phrases.english: Abaye said: Because of cracking.
phrases.notes: The crack may spread into the part of the bone that has meat on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical concern (a protective measure), not a disagreement in law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requires peeling to the joint because breaking a bone at a meat-free spot is itself forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Breaking at a meat-free spot is allowed in principle. The משנה forbids it only because the crack might spread into the meat-covered part.

steps.title: רבינא: the משנה is about a thigh bone
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the משנה is talking about a thigh bone (קולית), which is full of marrow. Breaking it is forbidden even where there is no meat outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It is talking about a thigh bone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different answer. The משנה is about a special kind of bone, so it does not contradict the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thigh bone has a lot of marrow inside. As step 4 taught, the איסור of breaking a bone covers a bone with marrow even if no meat is on the outside. So peeling a little would not help here, but for an ordinary bone without marrow, the rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The thigh bone, which has a lot of marrow inside

phrases.english: Ravina said: With a thigh bone.
phrases.notes: The marrow inside makes breaking it forbidden even with no meat outside.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule survives in two ways. אביי says the long procedure only prevents a crack from spreading. רבינא says the משנה is about a marrow-filled thigh bone, which may never be broken.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבינא's answer depends on the conclusion of step 4: the איסור of breaking a bone applies to a bone with marrow even when it has no meat outside.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the same קשיא that אביי answered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about any bone, so even a meat-free spot may not be broken.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a thigh bone full of marrow, which is forbidden to break for that reason. Ordinary bones follow the rule.

steps.title: A משנה: פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting a משנה from elsewhere: פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: פיגול and נותר (and טמא meat) make the hands טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes topic and quotes a משנה from another place. It is setting up the argument in the next step about the reason for this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, פיגול and נותר are disqualified but do not carry טומאה. The rabbis decreed that touching them makes the hands טמא. Because this is a rabbinic decree, the גמרא will next ask why the rabbis made it.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן disqualified by a wrong intention about when it would be eaten
קרבן meat left over past its time limit
Make the hands טמא (a rabbinic decree)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think פיגול and נותר are טמא by Torah law. They are only disqualified. The טומאה of the hands here is a rabbinic decree.

phrases.english: We learned there: Piggul and leftover meat (and impure meat)
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in parentheses and some don't.

phrases.english: make the hands impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, unrelated to the bone discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא by rabbinic decree.

steps.title: Two reasons for the decree: suspected priests or lazy priests
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree about why the rabbis made this decree. One says it is because of priests suspected of disqualifying קרבנות on purpose. The other says it is because of lazy priests.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree. One says: because of suspected priests. The other says: because of lazy priests.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different reasons for the decree in the משנה. The גמרא does not yet say which אמורא holds which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view: some כהנים might ruin a קרבן on purpose, by a wrong intention, to hurt its owner. Making their hands טמא punishes them and stops this. The second view: some כהנים might be too lazy to eat the meat on time, so it becomes נותר. Making their hands טמא pushes them to be careful.

keyTerms.meaning: One (of the two) said
Priests suspected of purposely disqualifying קרבנות
Lazy priests who let the meat become נותר

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Chisda disagree.
One said: Because of suspected priests.
phrases.notes: Priests suspected of ruining a קרבן on purpose to harm its owner.

phrases.english: And one said: Because of lazy priests.
phrases.notes: Priests too lazy to eat the meat before it becomes נותר.

steps.whyThisMatters: The two reasons may lead to different results in different cases. The גמרא will explore this next.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא. חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two competing reasons for the משנה quoted in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת about the reason for the decree: either to stop suspected priests from disqualifying קרבנות on purpose, or to push lazy priests to eat the meat on time.

steps.title: The two reasons are about two different items
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement between רב הונא and רב חסדא is resolved. One explains the decree on פיגול because of חשודי כהונה, and the other explains the decree on נותר because of lazy כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: One teacher explains the decree for פיגול, and the other explains it for נותר. The one who explains פיגול says the reason is כהנים suspected of ruining offerings on purpose. The one who explains נותר says the reason is lazy כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two אמוראים are not really arguing. Each one is giving the reason for a different item in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול only happens through a wrong intention, so the worry there is a כהן who ruins the קרבן on purpose. נותר happens when meat is not eaten in time, so the worry there is a כהן too lazy to eat it. Each reason fits its own case, so both reasons are correct.

keyTerms.meaning: teaches; here, gives his explanation about
כהנים suspected of ruining offerings on purpose
lazy כהנים who would not finish eating the meat

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one אמורא rejects the other's reason. Each reason is attached to a different case: פיגול or נותר.

phrases.english: One Sage taught it about piggul,
and the other Sage taught it about notar.
The one who taught it about piggul says:
It is because of suspect priests.
phrases.notes: Suspected of making a קרבן פיגול on purpose through a wrong intention.

phrases.english: And the one who taught it about notar says:
It is because of lazy priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר מַתְנֵי אַפִּיגּוּל, וּמַר מַתְנֵי אַנּוֹתָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent disagreement presented in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each opinion addresses a different item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree about one reason for the whole decree.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each gives the reason for a different item: חשודים for פיגול, lazy כהנים for נותר.

steps.title: Olive-size or egg-size: the minimum amount for the decree
steps.stepSummary: A second pair of views: the decree applies from a כזית, or only from a כביצה. The כזית view follows the size of the eating prohibition. The כביצה view follows the size for טומאה of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: One teacher says the decree applies to an olive-size piece, and the other says an egg-size piece. The one who says olive-size compares it to its prohibition. The one who says egg-size compares it to its טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another pair of teachings, this time about how much meat is needed for the decree to apply, and gives the reason for each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating פיגול or נותר is forbidden from a כזית, so one view copies that size. Food passes on טומאה only from a כביצה, so the other view copies that size, since the decree is about טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: the size of an olive; the amount for the eating prohibition
the size of an egg; the amount for food to pass on טומאה
its prohibition (against eating)
its ritual impurity

phrases.english: One Sage taught an olive-bulk,
and the other Sage taught an egg-bulk.
The one who taught an olive-bulk holds:
It follows its prohibition.
And the one who taught an egg-bulk holds:
It follows its impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר מַתְנֵי כְּזַיִת, וּמַר מַתְנֵי כְּבֵיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second detail about the same decree: the minimum size.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The minimum size for the decree is either a כזית, matching the eating prohibition, or a כביצה, matching the size for food טומאה.

steps.title: Did the rabbis make meat that left its area impure?
steps.stepSummary: The question is whether the טומאה decree also covers יוצא. Maybe it does not, because the worry of laziness does not apply there and כהנים would not take meat out on purpose. Or maybe all disqualified meat is the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Did the rabbis decree טומאה on meat that went out of its area, or not? Should we say they decreed טומאה on נותר because כהנים might get lazy about eating it? But meat that went out is different: כהנים would not take it out with their own hands, so the rabbis did not decree on it. Or perhaps there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about whether the decree also covers יוצא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the נותר decree was laziness, which is passive and easily happens. Taking meat out takes an active step, which כהנים would not do, so maybe no decree was needed. The other side says the rabbis made one rule for all disqualified קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: it was asked of them; an open question
קדשים meat that went out of its allowed area
taking it out actively, with one's own hands
perhaps there is no difference

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the decree is tied to its reason. The question is whether the rabbis' worry about lazy or suspect כהנים reaches a case that needs an active act.

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹצֵא גְּזַרוּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: Meat that went out: did the rabbis decree impurity on it or not?
Do we say:
Notar, on which they decreed impurity,
is because they might become lazy about it,
but meat that went out,

phrases.aramaic: אַפּוֹקֵי בְּיָדַיִם לָא מַפְּקִי לֵיהּ בְּיָדַיִם,
phrases.english: to take it out with their hands, they would not actively take it out,
so the rabbis did not decree impurity on it,
or perhaps there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason for the decree (lazy כהנים) to ask whether it reaches a new case, יוצא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rabbinic טומאה decree applies to יוצא, or only to פיגול and נותר.

steps.title: A limb that partly went out: cut it off at the joint
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if part of a limb went out, you cut down to the bone, peel the meat back to the joint, and cut it off there. This is the setup for a proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A limb, part of which went out. One cuts until reaching the bone, peels until reaching the joint, and cuts it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof by quoting a משנה about a limb that partly went out. The argument itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes that cutting off the part that went out saves the rest of the limb. Nothing in it suggests the inside part became טמא. That assumption is what the גמרא will use.

keyTerms.meaning: a limb
peels (the meat away from the bone)
the joint

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A limb, part of which went out,
one cuts until reaching the bone,
and peels until reaching the joint,
and cuts it off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question raised in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the rabbis made יוצא טמא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a limb that partly went out

steps.title: If it were impure, cutting it off would not help
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the part that went out were טמא. Then it would already have made the rest of the limb טמא by touching it, so cutting it off would accomplish nothing. This suggests the rabbis did not make יוצא טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the rabbis decreed טומאה on it, what is gained when one cuts it off? It already makes the rest impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its proof from the משנה: cutting off the outside part only makes sense if that part is not טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The part that went out is still attached to the rest of the limb. If it were טמא, it would make the inside meat טמא through contact, and the משנה's cutting method would save nothing. The משנה's instruction therefore points toward no decree on יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you say; introduces the opposite assumption to test it
what is gained? what difference does it make?
makes something impure

steps.confusionAlert: The worry is not that the cut-off piece is lost; it is lost anyway. The worry is that the attached טמא piece has already made the good part טמא before the cut.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה,
phrases.english: And if you say the rabbis decreed impurity on it,
when one cuts it off, what is gained?
It already makes it (the rest) impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the rabbis did not decree טומאה on יוצא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's method of cutting off the part that went out assumes the rest stays usable, which would fail if the outside part were טמא and touching it.

steps.title: The touching is hidden, so it passes on no impurity
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the limb is rejected. Even if the outside part were טמא, it touches the inside part only in a hidden place, and hidden contact does not make things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is impurity in a hidden place, and impurity in a hidden place does not make other things impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 15. It explains why cutting off the part that went out still helps, even if that part is טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said that if the outside part were טמא, it would already have made the rest of the limb טמא by touching it. The answer is that the two parts meet inside the flesh, where the contact cannot be seen. There is a rule that טומאת סתרים, contact in a hidden place, does not count. So the rest of the limb stays טהור, and the משנה proves nothing about יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity through contact in a hidden or concealed place
Does not make impure

phrases.english: It is impurity in a hidden place,
phrases.notes: The outside part and inside part touch only inside the flesh.

phrases.english: and impurity in a hidden place does not make things impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Step 15 by explaining why the rest of the limb is not made טמא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה of the limb that partly went out.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the touching would pass on טומאה. In fact it is hidden contact, which does not.

steps.title: For רבינא, the pieces really do touch
steps.stepSummary: רבינא holds that connected pieces of food count as separate pieces. If so, the outside piece simply touches the inside piece, and that touch should pass on טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבינא, who said that connections between foods are not a real connection and the pieces are like separate pieces, what can you say? They touch each other, and one makes the other impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the answer of Step 16 can work for רבינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 treated the limb as one connected piece, so the contact was hidden inside it. רבינא says connected food counts as separate pieces. Then the outside part and the inside part are two pieces touching each other. That is ordinary contact, not hidden contact, so the טומאה should pass, and cutting off the outside part would not help.

keyTerms.meaning: Connections between pieces of food
It is as if they were separated

phrases.english: And according to Ravina, who said:
connections between foods are not a real connection,
and they are like separated pieces,
what is there to say?
But they touch each other, and one makes the other impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 16 according to רבינא's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of טומאת סתרים in Step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If connected food counts as separate pieces, the contact is real touching between two pieces, not hidden contact. So טומאה should pass.

steps.title: The part that went out was too small
steps.stepSummary: For רבינא, a different answer is given. The משנה's case is where the part that went out is smaller than the size the decree requires: a כזית according to one view, a כביצה according to the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: according to the one who teaches a כזית, the case is where it does not have a כזית. And according to the one who teaches a כביצה, the case is where it does not have a כביצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to explain the limb משנה that works even for רבינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said the decree only applies from a minimum size, either a כזית or a כביצה. Here the משנה is explained as a case where the part that went out is below that size. Such a small piece never became טמא from the decree, so it could not make the rest טמא. This means the משנה still does not prove that יוצא is free of the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: Who teaches, meaning who holds this version
Olive-sized amount
Egg-sized amount
That it does not contain

steps.whatToRemember: The limb משנה proves nothing about יוצא. Either the contact is hidden, or, for רבינא, the part that went out was too small for the decree.

phrases.english: Rather: according to the one who teaches an olive-bulk,
the case is where it does not have an olive-bulk.
And according to the one who teaches an egg-bulk,
the case is where it does not have an egg-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17 by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a piece below the minimum size
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The part that went out was big enough to become טמא, so it should make the rest טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The part that went out was smaller than a כזית or a כביצה, so the decree never applied to it.

steps.title: A ברייתא about moving פסח meat between groups
steps.stepSummary: A new source is brought. Someone who moves קרבן פסח meat from one חבורה to another breaks a לא תעשה, yet the meat is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who takes meat of the פסח from one group to another group, even though he breaks a negative commandment, the meat is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to try again to answer the question about יוצא. It is setting up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח must be eaten in the place of the group that signed up for it. Moving it to another group's place breaks a לא תעשה. Still, the ברייתא says the meat stays טהור. The next step will try to use that word to prove the רבנן made no טומאה decree on יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: A group registered together to eat one קרבן פסח
A negative commandment
Ritually pure

phrases.english: Come and hear: one who takes out meat of the Paschal lamb
from one group to another group,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: even though he violates a negative commandment, it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַמּוֹצִיא בְּשַׂר פֶּסַח מֵחֲבוּרָה לַחֲבוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the limb proof fell, a new source is brought for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the רבנן decreed טומאה on יוצא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about moving פסח meat from one חבורה to another.

steps.title: Pure but forbidden, so no impurity decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as 'pure but forbidden.' Moving between groups counts as יוצא and disqualifies the meat, yet it is still called טהור, so the רבנן did not decree טומאה on יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that it is pure but forbidden? Meat that goes from one group to another is like meat that went outside its boundary, and it is disqualified. Even so, it teaches that it is pure. This shows the רבנן did not decree impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof out of the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on one assumption: that moving between groups is just like יוצא, so the meat is פסול. If so, this disqualified meat is still called טהור. That would show the טומאה decree does not cover יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that: introduces a suggested reading
Outside its allowed boundary
Becomes disqualified
This shows that
The רבנן decreed

steps.confusionAlert: Here טהור does not mean the meat may be eaten. The suggested reading is that the meat is pure but still forbidden, because it became פסול.

phrases.english: Is it not that it is pure but forbidden,
because meat that goes out from one group to another group
is like meat that went outside its boundary, and it is disqualified,
and even so it teaches that it is pure,
this shows that the Rabbis did not decree impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the ברייתא quoted in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן did not decree טומאה on יוצא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא calls the meat טהור even though moving it supposedly disqualified it.

steps.title: Moving between groups does not disqualify
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The ברייתא means 'pure and permitted,' because moving meat between groups is not like יוצא and does not disqualify it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No: it is pure and permitted, because meat that goes from one group to another is not like meat that went outside its boundary, and it is not disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from Step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on moving between groups being a real case of יוצא. The גמרא answers that it is not; the meat stays fully kosher even though a לא תעשה was broken. So calling it טהור tells us nothing about disqualified meat. The next step challenges this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted to be eaten
Is not like meat that went out

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common move in the גמרא. A proof is knocked down by rejecting the hidden assumption it was built on, without arguing with the source's words.

phrases.english: No: it is pure and permitted,
because meat that goes out from one group to another group
is not like meat that went outside its boundary,
and it is not disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 20 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא about moving meat between groups.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed moving between groups disqualifies the meat. In fact it does not, so the meat is simply pure and permitted.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא says eating the moved meat breaks a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection from step 21. The end of the ברייתא says that whoever eats the moved meat breaks a לא תעשה, so moving it must disqualify it as יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the end of the ברייתא teaches: whoever eats it breaks a לא תעשה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous rejection by quoting the end of the same ברייתא. It says that eating meat moved from one group to another is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 claimed the ברייתא means 'pure and permitted,' because moving meat between groups is not יוצא. The end of the ברייתא, however, forbids eating that meat, so the move clearly disqualifies it. That means the meat is יוצא, and calling it טהור seems again to show that there was no decree of טומאה on יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause or end of a teaching
The one who eats it
A Torah prohibition (a negative commandment)

phrases.english: But the latter clause teaches:
One who eats it violates a prohibition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the rejection in step 21 by using the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 21's reading that the ברייתא means 'pure and permitted.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If eating the moved meat breaks a לא תעשה, it is not permitted. So the move does disqualify it like יוצא, and step 21's reading collapses.

steps.title: The proof can be answered for the כביצה view but not for the כזית view
steps.stepSummary: For the view that the decree applies only to a כביצה, the ברייתא is a case of a כזית that is less than a כביצה. For the view that the decree applies even to a כזית, there is no way out.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says the decree needs a כביצה: the case is where the piece has a כזית but not a כביצה. But for the one who says the decree applies even to a כזית, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks whether the revived proof can be dodged. It can be dodged for one opinion but not for the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating breaks the לא תעשה only with a כזית, so the moved piece must be at least a כזית. If the decree requires a כביצה, the piece can be between a כזית and a כביצה, which explains why it is טהור. If the decree applies to a כזית, a forbidden piece should also be טמא, so calling it טהור remains a real difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable according to (one view)
The volume of an egg
The volume of an olive, the minimum amount that counts as eating
What is there to say? (there is no answer)

steps.confusionAlert: Two different measurements are in play. A כזית is the amount needed to break the prohibition by eating. The כזית or כביצה dispute is about how much meat the decree of טומאה covers.

phrases.english: It is understandable according to the one who says an egg-bulk:
the case is where it has an olive-bulk
but does not have an egg-bulk.
But according to the one who says an olive-bulk,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the revived proof against the two opinions about the decree's size introduced in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the רבנן decreed טומאה on יוצא, according to the view that the decree on disqualified קדשים applies from a כזית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The forbidden piece is at least a כזית. Under the כזית view it should then be טמא, yet the ברייתא calls it טהור.

steps.title: For פסח meat, the רבנן obviously made no decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא withdraws the earlier approach. For יוצא of קרבן פסח, it is clear the רבנן did not decree טומאה, because the members of the group are careful anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: about meat of the פסח that went out, we never had a question that the רבנן did not decree טומאה. Why? The members of a group are diligent and are very careful with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing what the question was about. For פסח meat, everyone agrees there was no decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree would have been a fence to keep people from letting sacred meat leave its place. The members of a פסח group are already very careful about this, so no extra fence was needed. The ברייתא calling moved פסח meat טהור therefore proves nothing about other sacrifices.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacred meat that left its permitted area
The רבנן decreed (a rabbinic enactment)
Members of the group eating one קרבן פסח together
Diligent, zealous

phrases.english: Rather:
regarding what went out of the Paschal lamb, we had no question
that the Sages did not decree impurity.
What is the reason?
Members of the group are zealous
and are very careful with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּיוֹצֵא בַּפֶּסַח לָא מִיבַּעְיָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unanswerable difficulty of step 23 by narrowing the scope of the original question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the question: the ברייתא about פסח is a special case and does not bear on the general question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא about פסח meat seemed to decide whether the רבנן decreed טומאה on יוצא in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: פסח is different, because the group's own carefulness made a decree unnecessary. The ברייתא proves nothing about other קדשים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common rabbinic idea: no fence (גזירה) is made where people are already careful.

steps.title: The real question is about other sacrifices, and it stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question was really about יוצא of other קדשים. The גמרא finds no answer and ends with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, our question was about other קדשים that went out. What is the law? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states what the real question was: other sacrifices that left their area. It then admits it cannot resolve it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With פסח set aside as an obvious case, the only open question is about other קדשים, where people may be less careful. No source settles it, so the matter is left open as תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial meat in general
We were asking (this was our question)
Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: For קרבן פסח, the רבנן did not decree טומאה on meat that went out, because the group is careful. For other קדשים, whether there is such a decree is unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Rather, when we asked
it was about sacrificial meat that went out: what is the law?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לַן בְּיוֹצֵא בְּקָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reframing begun in step 24 and closes the investigation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether the רבנן decreed טומאה on יוצא of other קדשים remains a תיקו.

steps.title: Opening a new question about carrying פסח meat out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new discussion about someone who carries פסח meat out of its group, looking for the source of that law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who carries out meat of the פסח...
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא starts a new topic: where we learn the prohibition against carrying פסח meat out of its group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous investigation is finished. The גמרא now turns to the law it cited earlier, that moving פסח meat breaks a לא תעשה, and will ask for its source. The question itself continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries out
Meat of the קרבן פסח

phrases.english: And one who carries out meat of the Paschal lamb

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic, taking up the law about moving פסח meat that was mentioned in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the לא תעשה against carrying פסח meat out of its group (completed on the next amud).
